title: Communication-aware motion and coverage planning
description: Coverage planning considers the changing radio links and information-exchange opportunities created by moving UAVs.
introduction: Where a UAV flies changes the network it can use, and the available network changes how well a team can cooperate. This research connects communication awareness with motion and coverage planning, allowing robots to explore while creating useful opportunities to exchange information.

problem.heading: Plan around information arriving intermittently.
paragraphs: Aerial robot teams use shared maps and teammate information to coordinate their motion. Distance and obstacles continually change radio quality, so useful information may arrive late or be temporarily unavailable.

Maintaining a useful team therefore involves more than planning each vehicle’s coverage path. The motion plan also influences when robots can exchange information and reconnect their knowledge of the mission.

approach.heading: Bring communication and motion into the same plan.
paragraphs: The communication and motion awareness survey organizes approaches to this coupled problem. It provides a broader framework for understanding how aerial teams account for the network while coordinating motion.

SpArC-NARTs plans coverage trajectories offline using simulated annealing. It accounts for energy, sensing uncertainty, prior information and expected radio performance, balancing exploration with opportunities for information exchange.

Inês Marques and Meysam Basiri’s connectivity-aware coverage paper is a separate contribution. It uses simulated annealing for multi-UAV coverage planning with connectivity considerations and retains its own authorship and publication record.

evidence.label: Published research framework
evidence.text: The project includes a published survey, the SpArC-NARTs coverage-planning framework and a distinct connectivity-aware coverage contribution. Their publication records and authors remain separate.
